name: Talking About Crane: Seven Accounts
author: Collected by an unnamed researcher; circulated in the freelancer community
description: A compiled oral history circulating in physical copy among mid-to-high Signal freelancers, passed hand to hand rather than distributed through any network node. The collector is not identified. Each account was gathered separately; subjects were told only that someone was 'asking about Crane.' The document has no publication date. Several pages of a known copy show water damage. Some in the community believe the collector is themselves a freelancer. Others think the collector is dead.
body:
TALKING ABOUT CRANE: SEVEN ACCOUNTS [collector's note: I have edited for length only. I have not corrected contradictions. That is the point.]

---

I. MACE, B-TIER FREELANCER, CURRENTLY OPERATING OUT OF THE NARROWS, SECTOR 11

This was seven years back, maybe eight. A retrieval job out of the Gray Zone 4 district, the old pharmaceutical complex they'd converted into residential before the conversion stopped halfway through and it turned into something else entirely. We were three on the job. Me, a woman called Setter, and Crane.

Crane was — okay. Medium height. Broad through the shoulders, which surprised me because the hands were small. I remember the hands specifically because I watched them the whole job. You do that, you watch hands. Left hand was chrome to the elbow, older model, not flashy, the kind you buy used twice over. Right hand was flesh. Hair cut short on one side, longer on the other, dark. I never got a clear look at the face because Crane didn't want me to. That sounds dramatic but it wasn't — it was just practical. The body language said: don't study me. So I studied the hands.

We got the package. We got out. Crane was already gone by the time Setter and I cleared the exit corridor. That's not a metaphor. I mean physically gone. We looked at each other and we both shrugged. We got paid. I never heard from Crane again directly but I heard about the work, after.

---

II. BROKER, IDENTITY WITHHELD, OPERATING SOMEWHERE IN THE CANOPY ADJUNCT

I have processed work attributed to Crane on three separate occasions over the course of approximately five years. I say attributed because I cannot confirm identity. That's the whole problem and also the whole point.

The first job: clean. Outcomes matched contract terms exactly. The dead drops used were in locations I'd never seen anyone use before, which told me something — either extreme paranoia or prior operational history in sectors I don't usually touch.

The second job: also clean, but there was a note left with the token. Handwritten. It said the secondary target had been a juvenile and had been left untouched, and that the contractor should be aware of this discrepancy in their intelligence. No apology. No complaint. Just information.

The third job I will not describe in detail. I'll say this: the outcome was clean. The method was not something I want to repeat as a commission. I processed the tokens and closed the file and I didn't ask questions because questions are a thing you do when you want answers and I did not want answers.

I have never met Crane. I do not want to. I have enormous respect for the work.

---

III. SUBJECT DECLINES NAME, DECLINES TIER IDENTIFICATION

You want to know what it's like? It's like being very cold. That's the thing nobody tells you. I was in a building — I won't say which one — and I knew someone was there who was not supposed to be there, and then I knew that someone was specifically there for me, and the way I knew was just cold. Like a window opened somewhere. I checked all the windows. They were closed.

I got out. I don't fully understand how I got out. I made decisions very fast and some of them were luck and some of them were — I used to think I was smart. I don't think that anymore.

Crane didn't follow me out of the building. I think Crane let me go. I don't know why. I have spent three years thinking about why and I have no answer that makes me feel better. The not-knowing is its own thing I carry around.

I changed everything after that. Sector, affiliation, everything. I don't know if it helped. I still feel cold sometimes in rooms I know are warm.

---

IV. PELLAMO, C-TIER FREELANCER, SHELF 2

I was going to die. I want to be plain about that — I have talked to people who exaggerate these things and I am not exaggerating. I was in the Narrows elevated market, the one on 7th spur, and I had made a mistake with some people who do not forgive mistakes, and there were three of them and I had nothing useful.

Somebody intervened. I did not see it happen the way you see a thing. I heard it. Then the three people were not a problem anymore and I was bleeding from my arm but I was not dead.

I saw a person walking away. Medium height. I called out — I don't know why, shock probably — and the person turned around. I couldn't see the face clearly. One arm caught the light different than the other.

They said: get that looked at, pointing at my arm. Then they left.

I asked around after. Somebody told me that sounded like Crane. I didn't believe it at first because why would Crane — I'm nobody. I'm still nobody. But nothing else explains it and I've stopped trying.

---

V. DEVEREAUX-OKAI, A-TIER FREELANCER, SECTOR 7 OPERATING RANGE

I think Crane is four people. Maybe five.

Look at the timeline. Look at the geography. There are confirmed sightings — or what people call confirmed — in Sector 3 and Sector 14 within the same week, twice. Sector 3 to 14 is six hours minimum, bad traffic. I've made that run. You don't do it twice in a week unless you're running hot and stupid.

What I think happened: there was a real person, maybe still is, maybe not, who built the name up. And then the name became useful for other people to borrow. Maybe with permission, maybe not. Maybe Crane is a brand now. A signal that certain kinds of work come with certain standards.

That's not less interesting, actually. That's more interesting. It means something about how reputation operates outside the vouching structure. It means the work can be the identity.

I'm not saying this to be dismissive. I'm saying it because I think it's more likely and also more frightening than one person.

---

VI. NAME UNKNOWN, VOICE RECORDING ONLY, BACKGROUND NOISE SUGGESTS SHELF DISTRICT

I only said I'd talk because you came through a person I trust. I want that on record.

Crane is real. One person. I know this. I cannot tell you how I know.

Crane has done things I cannot justify and things I cannot explain and at least one thing that I think about — I think about it as something like grace. That's a weird word for this world. I know. But I don't have a better one.

I'm not going to say more than that. I'm sorry. It's not that I don't trust you. It's that some things get people killed by being said out loud and I would like to not be killed.

Crane is real. That's what I came to say.

---

VII. [HANDWRITTEN ADDITION, DIFFERENT INK, FOUND IN ONE CIRCULATING COPY ONLY]

I have read all of this.

Some of it is right. Some of it is wrong. The part about the hands is right.

I'm not going to tell you which parts are wrong. You can probably figure out why.

I would ask whoever made this not to circulate it further but I understand that request is useless by now. Things get out. That's the whole lesson, isn't it. Things get out.

Take care of yourselves.

---

[collector's final note: I have not been able to determine who wrote the handwritten addition. I have compared it against no known samples because there are no known samples. I am choosing not to try harder than I already have. Some research has a natural stopping point and you know it when you reach it.]
